title: Partial Object Initialization (Semantic Coupling)
pattern: A function accepts a large, complex struct argument but only reads a tiny subset of its fields, forcing callers to instantiate the whole struct (often filling unused fields with dummy values).
why_bad: It introduces semantic coupling. The calling function depends on the entire structural layout of the complex struct. If unrelated fields change or require complex setup, the caller breaks.
detection: Functions where a parameter struct is passed, but static analysis shows only a small fraction of fields (e.g., < 25%) are ever read in the function body.
counterexample: Structs passed to generic framework adapters or serializers that automatically inspect and process all fields dynamically.
